subject: Dedicated reservation options & ramp — sizing and warmup for ZenOps POC
messages:
From: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@zenops.ai>
To: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Dedicated reservation inquiry — sizing and ramp for Proof-of-Concept

Hi Sean,

Thanks for taking the meeting earlier. As discussed, we're kicking off a 3-month POC to evaluate a dedicated inference lane for our conversational agent. High-level asks: predictable latency under 200ms p95, a minimum committed capacity we can rely on for SLA testing, and a clear ramp plan into production if the POC meets our goals.

Some context: typical inference pattern for the POC will be ~120 concurrent sessions, average context 1.2k tokens, and bursts up to ~300 concurrent sessions during peak tests. We're open to different model sizes (13B and a slim 7B quantized variant). Budget target for committed costs during the POC is roughly $40k/month.

Can you send a few reservation options (cluster sizing, min GPUs, warmup plan) and any recommendations around prewarming/cache strategies and canary timelines? Also include any constraints we should be aware of for model quantization or KV cache priming.

Appreciate it — Ethan
ZenOps (product)

Attachments: ZenOps_RFP_Q2-2025.pdf (document stub)

From: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
To: Ethan Cole <ethan.cole@zenops.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2025 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation inquiry — sizing and ramp for Proof-of-Concept

Ethan — thanks for the clear context. Attached is a concise set of reservation options tailored to the POC (PDF). Below is a short summary and recommended warmup/runbook so your SRE and ML teams can plan.

High-level constraints we used: 200ms p95 aim, mixed 13B / quantized 7B workload, peak concurrency 300 sessions. Recommendations assume use of automatic KV prefix caching for session reuse and continuous batching in the serving runtime.

Option 1 — Pilot lane (low-commit)- Minimum commit: 4 GPUs (A10G-equivalent or better)- Configuration: 2 nodes x 2 GPUs, dedicated serving group with prefix cache enabled- Ramp: 1 week activation, 2-week canary (50% traffic), scale to full after validation- Burst: up to +2 GPUs on demand (subject to availability)- Expected POC monthly committed cost (est): $18k- Notes: Good for fast validation; may hit p95 at very high concurrency unless batching windows increase.

Option 2 — Production-onramp (recommended for your peak tests)- Minimum commit: 12 GPUs- Configuration: 3 nodes x 4 GPUs or 4 nodes with mixed 2/4 depending on availability- Ramp: Week 0: reserve and prewarm (KV priming scripts)
  Week 1–2: canary at 40–60% load, latency & quality checks
  Week 3–6: phased activation to full capacity with monitoring and autoscaling buffer- Burst: +6 GPUs from shared pool for 2–4 hour peaks; warm standby configured- Expected POC committed cost (est): $45k/month (we can discuss discounts)- Notes: Targets your 300-concurrency burst with headroom for quantized 7B; better p95 stability and fewer cold starts.

Option 3 — Anchored capacity (enterprisey, longer-term)- Minimum commit: 32 GPUs- Configuration: multi-rack, balanced KV cache sharding, redundant availability zones- Ramp: 4–8 week staged activation with SLA-backed throughput targets- Burst: +20 GPUs across regions for geo-bursting- Expected monthly committed cost (est): $120k+ (custom terms)- Notes: Only recommended if you intend to move large production traffic quickly. We include higher SLA and warmup credits.

Warmup and prewarming suggestions- KV cache priming: run synthetic runs to populate common prefixes before canary cutover- Model warmup: run 1–2k inference prompts per variant across all GPUs before traffic shift to populate attention caches- Batching windows: use adaptive batching to keep latency under 200ms — we recommend starting with 25–40ms batching windows during canary

Operational recommendations- Canary targets: functional (output quality), latency (p95 < 200ms), cost per token baseline- Fallbacks: policy to fallback to hosted model variant if dedicated capacity is saturated (we can enable automatic fallback)- SLA testing: we provide a simple runbook for load testing and error monitoring (attached).

Pricing & incentives- For POC: we can offer 1 week of warmup credits and an introductory 10% rebate on committed spend for the first quarter if you sign up for a 6-month minimum on Option 2 or 3.

Next steps- If Option 2 looks right, we'll send a short SOW + activation timeline and a draft reservation term sheet (DocuSign). Happy to jump on a 30-min call with your infra lead to align the canary checklist.

—Sean
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Quick internal note / cc'ing Ethan so he's aware of our ask:

Sean — nice summary. A few items to add before we send the SOW:

1) Minimum GPU floor: for mixed workloads (13B + quantized 7B) recommend stating a floor of 6 GPUs in the SOW for fast failover when prewarming fails — this covers model memory skew and short-term spikes.
2) Security/compliance: Ethan, we will include a short appendix describing VPC peering, customer-managed KMS for checkpoint protection, and audit log retention options (30/90/365 days). Please flag if you need SOC2 attestation language in the SOW.
3) Commercial: propose a 10% POC rebate as Sean suggested; also add a 30-day exit notice if the POC does not convert.

I'll work with Karthik to convert Option 2 into a SOW draft with explicit activation milestones and acceptance criteria (latency p95, throughput tests, quality pass-rate on 200 eval prompts). Karthik — can you add a short tech appendix about KV shard sizing and node placement?

—Marissa
Director, Solutions Engineering, Redwood Inference

From: Priya Rao <priya.rao@zenops.ai>

Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation inquiry — sizing and ramp for Proof-of-Concept

Thanks — this looks helpful. ZenOps is inclined toward Option 2 (12 GPUs) to make sure our peak tests are representative of production. A few asks before we sign the SOW:

1) Can you provide an explicit week-by-week activation schedule (we prefer a one-page timeline to include in our change board)?
2) We need the SOW to include the warmup checklist and the exact acceptance test (we'll run the 200-eval prompts and a 6-hour sustained 250-concurrency run).
3) Please attach the POC commercial term sheet (monthly committed fee + overage pricing) and the DocuSign link for signatures.

If you can send the SOW + timeline and price sheet by EOD Tuesday, we'll review and aim to get this into our change board for a decision next Wednesday.

Best — Priya
Head of Engineering, ZenOps
